Q: different between cmpxchg and btr bts A:

lock bts [mem], 0 costs about the same as lock cmpxchg on all CPUs. (https://uops.info/ and https://agner.org/optimize/). Any differences are only a couple uops of microcode for instructions that take ~20.

bts / btr are just basically TAS (test-and-set). Only usable for locking, or limited lock-free use-cases.

cmpxchg is CAS, compare-and-swap, a basic building-block for lock-free atomic operations. Any arbitrary atomic-RMW can be implemented using a CAS retry loop, for example an atomic right shift. (shr [mem], imm8 doesn't support a lock prefix.) Or an atomic double-precision multiply if you transfer the FP bit-pattern to/from integer registers.

https://preshing.com/20120612/an-introduction-to-lock-free-programming/ has an example of a CAS retry loop for adding nodes to a linked list.

  • minimum required atomic instructions to support C++11 concurrency libraries

  • Why does C/C++ not have a atomic flag test_and_clear? - more about TAS as a historical locking primitive. x86 does have test-and-clear with lock btr, but some ISAs like m68k only had TAS.

  • How is atomic_flag implemented? (usually with xchg because that's slightly more efficient than lock bts for storing a 1 and loading the old value, on existing CPUs.)

  • Is x86 CMPXCHG atomic, if so why does it need LOCK? - bts or cmpxchg without a lock prefix are useful on unicore machines, or if memory is only shared between a thread and a signal/interrupt handler which interrupts that thread. In that case atomicity wrt. interrupts is sufficient, and x86 guarantees that interrupts are delivered at instruction boundaries. (Like most but not all ISAs, notably m68k.)

Q: Does the returned value from `std::steady_clock::now()` denote a point in global time of the program? A:

[time.clock.req]p2:

In Table 131 C1 and C2 denote clock types. t1 and t2 are values returned by C1​::​now() where the call returning t1 happens before ([intro.multithread]) the call returning t2 and both of these calls occur before C1​::​time_point​::​max().

Expression Return type Operational semantics
C1::is_steady const bool true if t1 <= t2 is always true and the time between clock ticks is constant, otherwise false

So if #2 happens before #3, you can know that now1 <= now2.

This implication does not run backwards. From now1 <= now2, you can not deduce that #2 happens before #3. You can only say that now1 < now2 implies #3 does not happen before #2, but they could be unsequenced.

Q: Easy way to switch between accounts on git in the terminal on windows? A:

You can associate different credentials with each of your repos and have that automatically just work on git command line.

As per Git Credentials docs, I added this to each repo's .git/config:

[credential "https://github.com"]
    username = the_github_username_here

And then git uses the specified username for each repo.

I did first have to follow instructions to remove github credentials from Credential Manager. Perhaps this was because it had saved a credential under the address

git:https://github.com

instead of the more specific addresses

git:https://the_relevant_username@github.com

My experience is that after doing this in each repo, github shows me a 'please authenticate' dialog at my next push, once per repo, and after that seamlessly uses windows credential manager, which has now remembered each github credential separately:
